scope: Final blocking stock-count persistence review and targeted correction; source and automated tests only for this agent.
rootCause: setStockLevel wrote an absolute count to SQLite before separately creating audit/outbox work.
pushWriteInBackground ignores its legacy write callback, so mysqlSetStockLevel(expectedStockLevel) was never the active native path.
The queued full-product snapshot could replay a stale absolute stock value and overwrite another till's sale.
Even metadata-only patches queued full product snapshots containing cached stockLevel.
correction: Standalone counts use the existing native commit_local_batch command with the new setStock mutation: signed 32-bit integral count and expected value, UPDATE compare-and-set and audit in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction.
setStock mutations cannot create an absolute outbox upload.
Shared counts are online-only and flush then reject remaining product/sale/receipt queue work, matching quarantined stock conflicts or online financial recovery intents.

The pinned MariaDB transaction locks close barrier, signed restore gate, dataset epoch and product before checking expected stock; only stockLevel and updatedAt change, and the stock_counted audit commits in that transaction.
Changed stock rolls back without a count/audit write and attempts guarded stock-only cache refresh before reporting the conflict.
Uncertain COMMIT reports that the count outcome is unconfirmed and explicitly says not to repeat it.
Confirmed server count is not reported as failed if cache refresh fails; confirmed standalone count is also preserved if the post-commit display read fails.

The native server-count cache mirror requires the same dataset epoch, unchanged local stock and updatedAt, and no pending or quarantined product/sale/receipt work; accepted cache stock only is published to the product store.

Catalogue reviewer added the narrow commerce.rs generic-upsert guard: stockLevel cannot update an existing product through metadata replay; new product INSERT retains initial stock. Dedicated sales and receipts are unaffected.

tests.focusedResult: Initial full run: 24 passed (21 production-orchestration checks plus 3 exact-production-SQL checks against disposable MariaDB). Final hardening run without the now-shut-down scratch server: 23 orchestration checks passed, 3 real-SQL checks skipped. Combined evidence covers all 26 cases; the authority SQL is unchanged by the final local-cache/conflict hardening.
orchestrationCases: Pinned lock/CAS/audit order and publication from accepted cache only
Sale after editor opening causes conflict, no count/audit write, observed-stock refresh
Offline shared count rejected without queueing
Unresolved quarantined stock synchronization conflicts rejected
Audit failure causes rollback before cache work
COMMIT transport failure explicitly prohibits repetition and creates no local retry
Confirmed server commit survives local cache-refresh failure
Standalone count and audit share one native CAS batch with no upload row
Standalone post-commit display-read failure cannot report a failed count or invite repetition
Browser preview uses local CAS and no SQL/native IPC
No-op count accepts zero changedRows and preserves audit
realMariaDbCases: Exact production transaction SQL commits stock and audit while preserving product name and price
Exact production stale-count rollback branch leaves stock and audit unchanged
Real duplicate-audit insertion failure rolls back the preceding stock update
tests.nativeResult: 18 passed, including three new stock-specific test groups; four pre-existing dead-code warnings.
newNativeGroups: Successful CAS+audit; stale expected count rejected; failed audit rolls count back; metadata retained; no upload created
Missing product, fractional values, integer overflow and queued absolute counts rejected
Server cache mirror accepts clean baseline; rejects changed stock, changed timestamp, replaced/missing epoch, product queue, sale bundle, receipt bundle and quarantined product/sale/receipt conflicts
tests.typecheck: npm run check: 0 errors, 0 warnings; Tauri command audit passed (95 frontend commands, 101 registered).
tests.independentReview: Catalogue agent independently source-reviewed lock order, CAS/audit transaction, stock-only guarded cache mirror and standalone atomicity; no new blocker found.
tests.scratchSafety: Used only explicitly provided socket-only disposable MariaDB. Generated pos_test_count_<pid> schema was dropped after tests. No shop credentials, app database or real payment operations used. Catalogue reviewer subsequently confirmed shutdown of the exact scratch server and removal of its socket.

limits: Original source-author evidence did not control native UI; the later root nativeSupplement records the healthy count/restoration only. Neither scope claims a blanket native stale/error PASS.
Shared stock counts are intentionally unavailable offline; metadata edits retain their existing durable queue behavior.

Legacy queued full-product rows cannot distinguish an old absolute count from a metadata snapshot. Existing-product replay intentionally ignores their stock, protecting authoritative stock; old pending counts require review/recount rather than blind replay.
No new native command, capability, build feature or permission is needed.
The real MariaDB checks execute SQL captured from production orchestration; SQL/IPC boundary decisions are separately covered by the production-function VM fixture and native SQLite tests.

nativeSupplement.scenario: Native Save Item counted stock 0→1 with item tracking on, confirmed UI/database result and zero queue/conflicts/intents; second save restored stock 1→0, item tracking off and price 169p. Global stock tracking was restored off.
nativeSupplement.limits: Healthy native count/save/restoration only. Native stale/error, audit rollback, uncertain COMMIT and cache-failure branches were not fault injected; automated/source evidence above covers those boundaries. Details and stock remain separate commits.
